primitives.name: Dribble Hand-Off Classification
primitives.verbatim_quote: One of the most effective actions in dynamic offensive strategies in basketball is the dribble hand-off (DHO).
primitives.assumptions: Player movements are captured via SportVU tracking data; DHOs are defined as coordinated actions involving two offensive players and a ball handler.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When player trajectories deviate from standard screen-cut patterns or involve fake execution signals.

layer2.mapping: DHO classification maps to supervised learning models trained on hexbin-encoded player path features, aligning with GSI's probabilistic event labeling framework.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of DHO variant prediction from hexbin trajectory inputs.

primitives.name: Hexbin Trajectory Encoding
primitives.verbatim_quote: This pipeline consists of a combination of player tracking data and event labels, a rule set to identify candidate actions, player trajectories embedded into hexbin cell paths, and passing the completed training set of generated features to the classification and clustering models.
primitives.assumptions: Player movement data is discretized into hexagonal bins to preserve spatial continuity and reduce noise.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At low-resolution tracking data or high-density player clustering scenarios.

layer2.mapping: Hexbin encoding serves as kernel for feature extraction in DHO detection pipelines, enabling GSE's spatial reasoning engine to interpret motion paths.
layer2.telemetry: Spatial resolution fidelity of hexbin bins relative to actual player displacement.

primitives.name: On-Ball Screen Variant
primitives.verbatim_quote: There are many versions of the screen, each with several additional variants, but perhaps the most common is the on-ball screen.
primitives.assumptions: On-ball screens are characterized by a ball-handler and screener with distinct positional roles and timing.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When screen execution fails due to miscommunication or defensive disruption.

layer2.mapping: On-ball screen logic mirrors DHO structure in terms of coordination and intent, supporting cross-action comparative analysis in GSI's event taxonomy.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency and success rate of on-ball screen implementations across game states.

The core operational principle of this work lies in transforming continuous player trajectory data into structured hexbin representations, which are then fed into classification models. The DHO action is mathematically framed as a temporal-spatial event composed of two interacting agents (ball handler and screener), where the system identifies a set of candidate actions based on predefined rules. These candidates are encoded into hexbin paths, forming a discrete feature space. Supervised learning algorithms are applied to classify these actions into variants such as pick-n-roll or fake DHOs. The breakdown regime occurs when the hexbin resolution is insufficient to distinguish subtle variations in movement, or when the rule set fails to capture non-standard execution patterns. The failure mode arises from overfitting to training data or underrepresentation of rare variants in the dataset. Dualities emerge between the hexbin encoding and the underlying geometric structure of court space, allowing for robust pattern mining. The system’s reliability hinges on the consistency of tracking data and the generalizability of the learned classifiers.
